revisions.summary: Prior-year lobster import declared customs value corrected from $8.99 to $9.00 a pound, in the table and in the text.
revisions.detail: The stored value is 8.995 and rounds to $9.00. tools/issue.py formatted a float, and the nearest double to 8.995 is just below it, so a figure whose exact decimal fell on a half printed one unit low; tools/check.py rounded the same way and so agreed with it. Both now round half away from zero on the decimal through common.round_half_up. The percentage change beside the figure, +0.3%, is computed from unrounded values and was correct in version 1.0. No other figure in this issue changed. The defect was found by editorial review of the Egg & Butter Brief's first issue and is recorded in PROVENANCE.md.

standard: Field Assembly Record Standard 1.2, §8 market records; see PROVENANCE.md
notes: Numbers computed from run 2026-10-18T144903Z and recomputed after two corrections to the record's tooling and two additions to the computed set. The BLS PPI and CPI series carry September 2026. Prose drafted 2026-10-18 by a session from numbers.md at the editor's instruction, then revised on editorial review, which recalculated every figure from the captured sources, confirmed the arithmetic, and required eight changes: one factual error, "within a point and a half" for a 2.687-point difference, and seven passages claiming more than the measurements establish. tools/check.py passes at 76 figures. Corrections to the record's tooling before this issue was computed. The 2026-10-01 observation pass had captured all eight sellers and the record carried rows for one: a seller behind a bot check served an HTML captcha with a 200 to its product endpoint, the parser called json.loads on it, and the resulting JSONDecodeError was not a ParseFailure, so it ended the pass instead of failing that source, costing the six sellers after it in source order. lobster/observations/tools/parse.py now fails a source rather than the pass, and the retained captures were re-parsed. The month holds both capture dates and every seller's 2026-10-01 outcome is explicit in the observation record's flags: two parsed, two parse failures, four capture failures from one HTTP 403 and three HTTP 429. The four lost at capture are not recoverable from the retained response and their listings are marked unavailable for that date rather than omitted. Separately, issue.py built its series map from the named run alone, which does not affect this title, whose sources carry their own history; it is recorded in PROVENANCE.md. Additions to the computed set: the NOAA import measures are labelled as declared customs value for the Portland ME customs district, which is what the source publishes, and retail_reference now records comparable_series_by_seller so the prose can attribute the comparable-series count. Known limits of this issue. Of the eight sellers observed, two list the reference series of a single live hard-shell 1.25 lb lobster, so the consumer reference rests on sellers D and G; G is observed on both capture dates and did not move, D on 2026-10-15 only. The consumer reference carries no year-over-year comparison: the observation record begins 2026-09-26. The NOAA import figures are for 2026-08 and the record holds no 2024-08 reading, so neither import measure carries a two-year comparison. The Maine DMR file is dated 2026-02-06 and ends with preliminary 2025 data. Month-to-month movement is not in this issue's computed set. The USDA ERS year-over-year attribute is August 2025 to August 2026. The verification gate does not read bare counts or worded quantities in prose; those were checked by hand against numbers.json.
